findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed no sanitizer to be set up upon arrival. Discussed with PIC, sanitizer solution was made and tested at 200 ppm Quat. Ensure a sanitizer solution is available at the proper concentration during all hours of operation.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(E) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (E) If a chemical SANITIZER other than chlorine, iodine, or a quaternary ammonium compound is used, it shall be applied in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions.

findings.title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed.

findings.citation_text: 5-402.13 Conveying Sewage. SEWAGE shall be conveyed to the point of disposal through an APPROVED sanitary SEWAGE system or other system, including use of SEWAGE transport vehicles, waste retention tanks, pumps, pipes, hoses, and connections that are constructed, maintained, and operated according to LAW.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

(REPEAT) Observed the sani buckets at the facility to be 100 ppm of quaternary ammonium. Discussed with both employees. Buckets were remade - 400 ppm. Ensure sani buckets are frequently remade in order to keep concentration of sanitizer at 200 to 400 ppm. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 3/30/22. COS. Facility has test strips to check concentration of sanitizer.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE. 

Observed the following areas in need of re-caulking: 3 compartment sink, mop sink basin, and one of the bathroom hand sinks (caulk is coming away from the sinks and walls). The metal prep table next to the fryers needs to be caulked. It is attached to the wall and therefore needs caulked to the wall. Discussed repairs with employees. Correct by next routine inspection.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria.

The sani buckets at the facility are observed between approximately 50-100 ppm quat. Buckets are observed at 1 quart and 2 quarts full respectively. New buckets were made, multiple amounts of solution were tested and  it appears that having more solution in the buckets increases the amounts observed on both the inspector’s and facility’s test strips. PIC was consulted and the procedure is being changed to four quarts solution (concentrations of 200+ ppm) per bucket moving forward. It is suggested that the facility should touch base with the company that maintains the system/ dispenser (EcoLab) and ensure that the equipment is functioning as intended.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. 

The paper towel rack in the bathroom is observed empty. Inspector discussed with the PIC and the towels were replaced during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.citation_text:
2-102.12 (A) (C) The person in charge shall be a certified food protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an accredited program.

During the inspection, the CFPM's shift ended and they left the property for the day. Their replacement did not have a certification from an accredited course available to view at the time of the inspection.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment:
750-130(e) Package food shall not be stored in direct contact with water or undrained ice.
750-120(a) Food shall be protected at all times. Properly store and protect food.
Observed 1) scoop stored in flour to be laying with the handle in the flour 2) a cup used as a scoop in a container of flour 3) ice from the condensers in both walk in freezers to be on containers of food beneath the condensers. Discussed the issues with the PIC and instructs 1) scoop to be stored with the handle sticking out or clean and dry in another location 2) use a scoop with a handle 3) prevent contamination of foods.

750-810b Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment: 750-160 Observed cartons of eggs being stored over milk and other ready-to-eat foods. Properly store food in their cooking orders. Do not store raw meats and egg over foods that require no further cooking.   Food shall be protected at all times from cross-contamination.

findings.title: Approved source
findings.comment:
Observed gravy dated 8/29 in the pizza prep cooler to be at 72 degrees F.  This gravy was used this morning and was put in cooler warm to be cooled and reheated tomorrow.  The breakfast burrito meat is also cooled and reheated.  A Medium Risk license does not allow for cooling and reheating of Potentially Hazardous Foods (PHFs).  Both the gravy and burrito filling were discarded and this practice will immediately stop per manager.  They will just heat up enough food to be used that day and discard any leftovers.  *Violation Corrected*
750-100 Food shall be obtained from sources that comply with all laws relating to food and food labeling.  The use of home prepared or home canned foods is strictly prohibited.
